# Prepare and file statutory annual accounts

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Geography](#geography) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Prepare the annual financial statements and complete the reporting obligations applicable to the entity and period.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source checked on 2026-11-01. No case-specific legal review, independent professional assurance or completed execution is claimed. The sources describe UK requirements; other jurisdictions need their own assessment.

> Scoped draft detail: UK-resident private company limited by shares registered in England and Wales, operating domestically in unregulated services. Other entities, locations and cross-border facts need another assessment. Professional review is pending. Source and instruction check: 2026-11-01. ## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Reconcile the entity reporting facts

agent-runnable


Collect the reporting period, entity records, reconciled ledger, ownership and prior filings. List the intended recipients and evidence still missing; a completed bookkeeping close does not establish statutory reporting completion.

- Sources: [GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts) · [GOV.UK accounts and tax returns](https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Confirm the reporting framework and obligations

human · human approval every run · hard to undo


The qualified accounting owner confirms the applicable reporting framework, available filing regimes, audit requirement and deadlines for the actual entity. Keep uncertain eligibility or obligations open and obtain specialist advice before choosing a filing route.

- Sources: [GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts) · [GOV.UK accounts and tax returns](https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the statements and supporting schedules

agent-runnable


Prepare statements, notes and reconciliations under the reviewed accounting instructions. Link balances to private records and identify judgments or omitted disclosures for the accountant rather than presenting a draft as approved accounts.

- Sources: [GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts) · [GOV.UK accounts and tax returns](https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve and sign the final accounts

human · human approval every run · hard to undo


The accountant and authorized corporate decision-makers review the complete statements and required signatures. Retain the approved version and resolve material errors before any submission or distribution.

- Sources: [GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts) · [GOV.UK accounts and tax returns](https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Distribute and file the approved statements

manual form/portal · human approval every run · hard to undo


Authorized operators use the applicable recipient and authority routes for the approved documents. Retain delivery evidence, submission references and any rejection; confirm the separate company-tax reporting work with its owner.

- Sources: [GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts) · [GOV.UK accounts and tax returns](https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company)

<a id="step-6"></a>

### 6. Verify acceptance and calendar the next reporting cycle

human · human approval every run · hard to undo


Reconcile accepted filings and required recipient deliveries to the approved statements. Assign corrections and outstanding obligations, retain evidence, and record the next reporting dates without treating a submission attempt as acceptance.

- Verify: Approved annual financial statements with required distribution and filing evidence, and unresolved exceptions assigned.
- Sources: [GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts) · [GOV.UK accounts and tax returns](https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company)

<a id="geo-uk"></a>

### United Kingdom

Scoped draft detail: UK-resident private company limited by shares registered in England and Wales, operating domestically in unregulated services. Other entities, locations and cross-border facts need another assessment. Professional review is pending.

- Scoped draft detail: UK-resident private company limited by shares registered in England and Wales, operating domestically in unregulated services. Other entities, locations and cross-border facts need another assessment. Professional review is pending. ([GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts))
- Step 1: Reconcile the entity reporting facts For the scoped active private company, reconcile the financial year, Companies House due date, HMRC accounting period and private accounting records. Dormant, group, charity or regulated accounts need another assessment. ([GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts))
- Step 2: Confirm the reporting framework and obligations The accountant confirms the reporting framework, eligible accounts regime, required reports and audit position. Use the actual first or subsequent reporting period; unresolved eligibility and disclosure questions require professional review. ([GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts))
- Step 3: Prepare the statements and supporting schedules Prepare the statements, supporting notes and reconciliations required by the reviewed regime. Keep the private full accounts and the version permitted for filing aligned, with any differences explicitly approved. ([GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts))
- Step 4: Approve and sign the final accounts Obtain the required director approval and signature on the final statements. The accountant checks reporting completeness and resolves material issues before the authorized person approves distribution and filing. ([GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts))
- Step 5: Distribute and file the approved statements Use the authorized Companies House filing route and deliver the required approved statements to their recipients. Coordinate the separate HMRC Company Tax Return, retain each receipt and handle rejection as unfinished work. ([GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts))
- Step 6: Verify acceptance and calendar the next reporting cycle Verify accepted filing and recipient delivery against the approved accounts. Record remaining corrections, preserve the signed statements and calendar the next accounts and tax reporting obligations separately. ([GOV.UK prepare annual accounts](https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts))
